texts.preamble: Manoj Kumar Agarwal Alias Manoj ... vs Ranchi Municipal Corporation Through ... on 13 October, 2017
texts.facts: The petitioner submitted his reply before the Ranchi Municipal Corporation vide letter dated 26.08.2017 stating, inter alia, that the sample of the edible oil taken by the State authorities from the trade premises of the petitioner was sent to the State Food Testing Laboratory, Namkum, Ranchi and as per its report dated 21.06.2017, it was found that the said sample corforms to the prescribed standard for refined palmolein, but the same has been found to be a misbranded one under Section 3(zf)(C)(i) of the Food Safety and Manoj Kumar Agarwal Alias Manoj ... vs Ranchi Municipal Corporation Through ... on 13 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103454368/ 1 Standard Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'the said Act') for which a proceeding has been drawn by the Deputy Commissioner, Ranchi under Section 52 of the said Act. It was further replied by the petitioner that Manoj Kumar Agarwal and Manoj Chhaparia are the same persons. The petitioner also submitted several documents in support of the said fact.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner has appeared in the said proceeding under Section 52 of the said Act and the reply would be filed soon before the Court of the Deputy Commissioner, Ranchi. It is further submitted that unless the proceeding under Section 52 of the said Act is concluded, the petitioner cannot be pre-judged to be guilty of misbranding of the edible oil. In the aforesaid circumstances, the impugned order dated 03.10.2017 whereby, the license of the trade premises of the petitioner has been cancelled by the Ranchi Municipal Corporation, Ranchi, is premature and arbitrary and, therefore, the operation of the said order may be stayed. Mr. Prashant Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the Ranchi Municipal Corporation and learned J.C to A.G pray for and are allowed four weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the petitioner has appeared in the said proceeding under Section 52 of the said Act and the reply would be filed soon before the Court of the Deputy Commissioner, Ranchi. It is further submitted that unless the proceeding under Section 52 of the said Act is concluded, the petitioner cannot be pre-judged to be guilty of misbranding of the edible oil. In the aforesaid circumstances, the impugned order dated 03.10.2017 whereby, the license of the trade premises of the petitioner has been cancelled by the Ranchi Municipal Corporation, Ranchi, is premature and arbitrary and, therefore, the operation of the said order may be stayed. Mr. Prashant Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the Ranchi Municipal Corporation and learned J.C to A.G pray for and are allowed four weeks' time to file counter affidavit.
